_note: Hand-written voice for the post-draft section. Generated numbers live in draft_analysis.json; nothing here is computed.
intro: One hundred sixty-eight picks. Twelve managers who all believe they nailed it. Every pick below is graded against FantasyPros' pre-draft Expert Consensus Rankings, normalised to this league's own trigger-happy pace, with kickers and defenses thrown out because ranking them 300th and then requiring everyone to draft one is how you end up calling a mandatory round-14 defense the worst pick of the night.

picks.Caleb Williams: Sixty-eight picks of value on a quarterback who will spend all fourteen weeks watching Trevor Lawrence from the bench. Immaculate process, zero points.
picks.KC Concepcion: The 160th pick of the draft returning WR113 value. At that stage most of the room was drafting kickers with their eyes closed.
picks.Dalton Kincaid: Round 11 for a top-90 tight end. He already had Jake Ferguson, so this is less a pick than a hostage situation for whoever needs a TE in October.
picks.Isaiah Likely: Round 11, ECR #91, and Bender didn't even need him. Just quietly hoarding assets like a man who read the room.
picks.Josh Jacobs: Bender took the actual starting running back at pick 80. Ploss had taken Jacobs' backup three picks earlier. Read that again.
picks.Drake Maye: QB3 by projection in round 6, and Campbell never had to touch his skill core to get him. The single best structural pick of the night.
picks.Travis Kelce: Round 9 for a name that used to go in round 2. Booker bought the nameplate at clearance and it might actually still work.
picks.Brock Purdy: A starting quarterback at pick 124. Topham spent rounds 1 through 10 exclusively on skill players and then just... had a QB. Rude.
picks.Tucker Kraft: Round 8, ECR #64, and Angelo needed a tight end. Sometimes the pick is just correct and there's nothing funny about it.
picks.Jakobi Meyers: Round 11 value on a receiver ranked 102nd. The one pick on Ploss's card that isn't actively arguing with the other picks.
picks.MarShawn Lloyd: The worst pick of the draft, and it's not close. Ninety-nine picks of reach on a handcuff whose entire value proposition is 'if Josh Jacobs gets hurt.' Dakota Bender then drafted Josh Jacobs three picks later. Ploss is holding the insurance policy on a car he does not own.
picks.Keenan Allen: ECR #215, taken 134th. Drafted a 34-year-old slot receiver in round 12 like it's still 2019 and he's still on the Chargers.
picks.T.J. Hockenson: Sixty-two picks early — and he's the starting tight end. Gamble reached into round 12 for the position he was going to have to start anyway.
Round 11, projects 67 points. That's four and a half points a week from a roster spot on the team with the league's worst receiving corps.
picks.Justice Hill: The 167th pick. Second-to-last selection of the entire draft, still somehow a forty-pick reach. Impressive in its way.
picks.Isiah Pacheco: Thirty-four picks early on a running back who is, at this moment, on injured reserve. The scouting report was written in pencil and the eraser was busy.
picks.Alvin Kamara: Torpey's fourth running back, taken 33 picks early, projecting 113. He can start two. The math has been alerted.
picks.Tre Tucker: Round 13, ECR #181. Lannon had the best roster in the league and spent the back half of his draft testing whether that was still true.
picks.Rashid Shaheed: Thirty picks early for Angelo's seventh receiver. At some point the WR room needs a bouncer.
picks.Matthew Golden: Round 8, ECR #127. The first of three straight reaches that turned a great draft into a merely good one.

teams.Tyler Scarlett: The board loved this draft more than the projections did — best expert grade in the league, sixth-best projected lineup. Forty-one percent of his starting points ride on Jeanty, Nabers and Henderson, three players the expert panel has separately flagged as likely to disappoint. Championship ceiling, trapdoor floor, no in-between. On brand for a man who went 3rd, 2nd, then 10th.
teams.Dakota Bender: The only roster both the experts and the model agree on — a disagreement gap of 0.04, the tightest in the league. Zero bust flags. Taylor and Barkley. He picked the year he owns the worst career average finish in league history to finally draft like a professional, which is the most Dakota Bender thing imaginable.
teams.Pj Lannon: Highest projected lineup in the league by 57 points and a C on the board. Nobody in this league splits the two views harder. He also has four starters on bye in week 11, and the luckiest career luck index on record, which regression has been circling for three years like a hawk with a spreadsheet.
teams.Jarett Coy: Owns the best running back room in the league and the worst receiving corps by 88 points, which sounds like a problem and is actually a business plan — RBs go twelve picks ahead of consensus here, so he's holding the one currency this league overpays for. The 83 points of trade upside is the most in the league. Executing it is a different sport.
teams.Dustin Gamble: Bijan and Jeremiyah Love is the best backfield in the league, and then he reached 62 picks for the tight end he was always going to start. Coming off the unluckiest season in league history — four wins on eight expected — which means last year's record was lying about him.
teams.Alex Topham: One quarterback, one tight end, nothing wasted, and a starting QB acquired at pick 124. The cleanest roster construction of the night, attached to the weakest running back room in the league. Puka Nacua's hamstring is the entire season.
teams.Angelo Hernandez: Josh Allen is the biggest single edge anybody bought — 48 projected points clear of the next quarterback. He then drafted seven wide receivers and three running backs in a format that starts two backs plus a flex. Three straight top-3 finishes says he knows something. The depth chart says he's one hamstring from the waiver wire.
teams.Corey Ploss: Second-best projected lineup, the league's best tight end, and the single worst pick of the draft. Forty-six percent of his starting points come from expert-flagged busts, which is the highest in the league and begins at pick 5 with a 30-year-old Christian McCaffrey. Fun team. Terrifying team.
teams.Andrew Campbell: The Drake Maye pick was the best structural decision anyone made. He is also the only manager in the league with zero tradeable running back surplus, on a roster whose biggest hole is at running back. Back-to-back titles in 2019 and 2020 are doing a lot of load-bearing work in these blurbs.
teams.Derek Booker: The defending champion drafted well by the board — A-minus, second-best expert grade — and the model put him dead last at 1,964 projected. That 2.43 disagreement gap is the second-widest in the league. He also has the worst defense in the league by 52 points, which is four points a week he simply chose not to have.
teams.Johnny Marcks: Best all-time win percentage in league history. Zero championships. Eleventh-place draft grade. Jefferson and Achane are excellent and then it falls off a cliff — Monangai 26 picks early, Pacheco on IR, and the second-weakest RB2 among the twelve. The Marv Levy tribute act enters its twelfth season.
teams.Kyle Torpey: Last in expert grade, last in the composite, and the only D on the board. Reached 33 picks for Kamara, 78 for Keenan Allen, and his best wide receiver — DK Metcalf at 196 projected — is stuck behind two others on his own bench. Renamed the team 'Bye Week' in 2023 and has finished 10th, 8th and 9th since. The name is not the problem, but it is being extremely honest.

tiers.name: The Contenders
tiers.blurb: One roster the experts adore and one the experts and the model actually agree on. Everyone else is playing for a bye.

tiers.name: Loaded, Pending Vibes
tiers.blurb: Genuine top-half talent attached to at least one structural flaw each — a bye-week crater, an empty receiver room, a tight end reached for in round 12. Any of these four wins it if the flaw stays quiet.

tiers.name: Mathematically Alive
tiers.blurb: Eight of twelve make the playoffs, so 'alive' is doing very little work here. All three have a real edge somewhere and a hole you could park a bus in somewhere else.

tiers.name: Already Watching Playoffs From Home
tiers.blurb: Contains the defending champion and the best regular-season manager in league history, which should tell you how much a draft grade is worth in September. It should also worry them.

Elimination scenarios arrive when they mean something, around week 5. Check back when someone has actually lost.
